
#======================================================================================================
Causal analysis of ecology, subsistence composition, and social organization in trans-historical small-scale farming societies using mixed-type Bayesian networks

## Subsistence variables are log-ratio transformed (ALR, Agriculture as reference)

Rosy Oh and Man-Suk Oh


Oct 25, 2026

#======================================================================================================

Pipeline
  1. Read data and pre-process
  2. Normalize (Yeo-Johnson) and standardize continuous variables
  3. Build the blacklist (forbidden arcs) from domain knowledge
  4. Learn BN structures on bootstrap samples with tpc() + mixCItest;
     Arc strength / direction; select arcs
  5. Build the consensus DAG
  6. Fit local models (lm for continuous nodes, multinom for discrete nodes)
  7. Interventional analysis via Monte Carlo simulation of do(Y)
  8. BIC of the consensus DAG

Required folders: data/ (input csv) and output/ (results). Run from the repository root.

# 0. Load packages
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readxl)
  library(pcalg)
  library(igraph)
  library(Rgraphviz)
  library(bnlearn)
  library(micd)
  library(tpc)
  library(nnet)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(GGally)
  library(httr)
})
```



# 1. Read data and pre-process
```{r}

# ── Analysis options ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# direction : blacklist scenario
#             "none"               no ordering between Subsistence and SocialOrg
#             "sub_to_soc"         Subsistence -> SocialOrg only
#             "soc_to_sub"         SocialOrg -> Subsistence only
# threshold : minimum arc strength for the consensus DAG
# B         : number of bootstrap replicates
direction=   "none"  #
threshold=0.3
B=10000


# Input data: first column = society ID, then 5 Ecology, 4 Subsistence and
# 4 SocialOrg variables (in this order)
dat.score=read.csv("data/dat_score_ALR_agri_157.csv",  header = TRUE)

names(dat.score)
dat.score=dat.score[, -1, drop=F]  # drop the Society ID column
Ecology=names(dat.score)[1:5]
Subsistence=names(dat.score)[6:9]
SocialOrg=names(dat.score)[10:13]
#summary(dat.score)



# Merge the "Camp" settlement type into "Hamlet"
dat.score$SettlementType[dat.score$SettlementType == "Camp"] <- "Hamlet"
dat.score$SettlementType <- factor(dat.score$SettlementType)

# Categorical social organization variables as factors
SocialOrg_categorical <- c("SettlementType", "CommOrg", "HouseholdOrg")
dat.score[SocialOrg_categorical] <- lapply(dat.score[SocialOrg_categorical], factor)

```


# 2. Normalize and standardize (mean 0, SD 1) continuous variables
```{r}
# Yeo-Johnson normalization (fn_normalize.R)
source("fn_normalize.R")
cols.conti <- which(sapply(dat.score, is.numeric))
res <- normalize(dat.score, cols.conti)

#res$summary     # lambda and Shapiro-Wilk p-values before / after
dat.trans=res$dat_trans   # transformed data

# Standardize
dat.trans[, cols.conti] <- scale(dat.trans[, cols.conti])

# Pearson correlations among continuous variables
cor_mat <- cor(dat.trans[, cols.conti], use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
cor_mat

```


# 3. Blacklist (forbidden arcs)
```{r}

# forb_all[a, b] = TRUE forbids the arc a -> b
# (scenario set by `direction` in Section 1)
#direction <- "none"
#direction <- "sub_to_soc"
#direction <- "soc_to_sub"


forb_all <- matrix(
  FALSE,
  nrow = ncol(dat.trans),
  ncol = ncol(dat.trans),
  dimnames = list(names(dat.trans), names(dat.trans))
)

# Ecology is exogenous: no arcs from Subsistence or SocialOrg into Ecology
forb_all[Subsistence, Ecology] <- TRUE
forb_all[SocialOrg, Ecology] <- TRUE

# Scenario-specific constraints between Subsistence and SocialOrg
if( direction == "sub_to_soc"){
   forb_all[SocialOrg, Subsistence] <- TRUE
} else if ( direction == "soc_to_sub"){
   forb_all[Subsistence, SocialOrg] <- TRUE
}
# if direction == "none" : no constraints 


# No arcs among subsistence variables: avoid spurious arcs induced by the common ALR reference (Agriculture)
forb_all[Subsistence, Subsistence] <- TRUE


diag(forb_all) <- FALSE

# Ecology hierarchy:
# Geography -> Topography -> Climate
Geography  <- c("DistanceCoast", "Elevation")
Topography <- "Slope"
Climate    <- c("AnnualTemp", "MonthlyPrecip")

# No arc between the two geographic variables (both directions forbidden):
# DistanceCoast and Elevation are both exogenous features of location, and
# neither causes the other.
forb_all["DistanceCoast", "Elevation"] <- TRUE
forb_all["Elevation", "DistanceCoast"] <- TRUE

# Forbid reverse directions within the hierarchy
forb_all[Topography, Geography] <- TRUE
forb_all[Climate, Geography] <- TRUE
forb_all[Climate, Topography] <- TRUE

# Arrange data and blacklist in exactly the same variable order
cols <- c(Ecology, SocialOrg, Subsistence)

dat <- dat.trans %>%   select(all_of(cols))

forb <- forb_all[cols, cols]

stopifnot(
  identical(names(dat), rownames(forb)),
  identical(names(dat), colnames(forb))
)

```


# 4. Learn BN structure on bootstrap samples; arc strength and arc selection
```{r}

# Fit a single BN to one bootstrap sample with tpc()
# (PC-type algorithm with the "stable" skeleton search; mixed data via mixCItest)
fit_one <- function(dat_sub, forb, alpha_level, numCores) {
  fit <- tpc(
    suffStat    = dat_sub,
    indepTest   = mixCItest,      # CI test for mixed continuous + categorical data
    labels      = names(dat_sub),
    alpha       = alpha_level,    # significance level of the CI tests
    forbEdges   = forb,           # blacklist matrix (domain constraints)
    maj.rule    = TRUE,           # majority rule for edge orientation
    skel.method = "stable",
    numCores    = 1
  )
  return(fit)
}

# ── Bootstrap settings ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(2374)

#B  : number of bootstrap replicates (set in Section 1)
p   <- ncol(dat)
vn  <- names(dat)
#numCores=1

# Storage: only DAGs that convert without cycles are kept
boot_nets        <- list()
successful_boots <- 0
skipped_boots    <- c()     # indices of replicates that failed conversion (e.g. cycles)

# ── Main bootstrap loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#cat("Starting bootstrap:", b, "/", B,
#    "at", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
#flush.console()

t0 <- Sys.time()

for (b in 1:B) {


  # Resample 80% of the observations (sampling with replacement)
  idx <- sample.int(
    nrow(dat),
    size = floor(0.8 * nrow(dat)),
    replace = TRUE
  )

  # Suppress near-singular covariance warnings from mixCItest() internals
  fit <- suppressWarnings(
    fit_one(dat[idx, , drop = FALSE],
            forb = forb,
            alpha_level = 0.1     )
  )

  # Convert to a bnlearn "bn" object; skip the replicate if it contains a cycle
  tryCatch({
    g <- as.bn(fit, check.cycles = TRUE)
    successful_boots <- successful_boots + 1
    boot_nets[[successful_boots]] <- g
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Bootstrap", b, "conversion failed:",
        conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    skipped_boots <<- c(skipped_boots, b)
  })

}
cat("Finished bootstrap:", b,
    "Elapsed:",
    round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0,
                              units = "secs")), 1),
    "seconds\n")
flush.console()

cat(sprintf("Completed: %d/%d replicates accepted (%d skipped)\n",
            successful_boots, B, length(skipped_boots)))

# ── Arc strength and direction (fn_calculate_arc_strength.R) ────────────────
source("fn_calculate_arc_strength.R")
arc_strength <- calculate_arc_strength(boot_nets, vn)

summary(arc_strength$strength) # strength and direction are both in [0, 1]



# ── Arc selection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Keep arcs with strength >= threshold and direction >= 0.5

#threshold   :given in Section 1
selected_arcs <- arc_strength[
  arc_strength$strength  >= threshold &
    arc_strength$direction >= 0.5, ]
print(selected_arcs)


# Save selected arcs and all arc strengths
fname=paste0("output/selected_arcs_", direction,"_thr", as.integer(threshold*10), ".csv")

write.csv(selected_arcs,fname , row.names = FALSE)

n_arcs <- nrow(selected_arcs);n_arcs

fname=paste0("output/arc_strength_", direction,"_thr", as.integer(threshold*10), ".csv")

write.csv(arc_strength,fname , row.names = FALSE)
```




# 5. Construct the consensus DAG from the selected arcs
```{r}

# Start from an empty graph on all nodes
avg_graph <- empty.graph(vn)

# Add selected arcs one by one, skipping any that would create a cycle
for (k in 1:nrow(selected_arcs)) {
  test_graph <- set.arc(avg_graph,
                        from         = as.character(selected_arcs$from[k]),
                        to           = as.character(selected_arcs$to[k]),
                        check.cycles = FALSE)

  if (acyclic(test_graph, directed = TRUE)) {
    avg_graph <- test_graph
  } else {
    message("Skipped arc: ", selected_arcs$from[k], " -> ",
            selected_arcs$to[k], " (would create cycle)")
  }
}

# Remove isolated nodes (keep only nodes involved in at least one arc)
connected_nodes <- unique(c(arcs(avg_graph)[, "from"], arcs(avg_graph)[, "to"]))
avg_graph <- bnlearn::subgraph(avg_graph, connected_nodes)
cat("Number of arcs in consensus DAG:", narcs(avg_graph), "\n")


# Keep a copy named by scenario, e.g. avg_graph_none
assign(paste0("avg_graph_", direction), avg_graph)


# Save / reload the consensus DAG (uncomment as needed)
#fname=paste0( "avg_graph_", direction,"_thr", threshold*10, ".rds")
#saveRDS(avg_graph, file =fname, compress = TRUE)

#avg_graph <- readRDS(fname)


# ── Plot the consensus DAG ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

gR <- graphviz.plot(avg_graph, shape = "rectangle")

if(direction == "sub_to_soc"){
  avg_graph_sub_to_soc=avg_graph
}else if (direction == "soc_to_sub"){
  avg_graph_soc_to_sub=avg_graph
}else if (direction == "none"){
  avg_graph_none=avg_graph
} 

# ── Node appearance ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
node.attrs <- nodeRenderInfo(gR)
arc.attrs  <- edgeRenderInfo(gR)

# Global node style
node.attrs$col     <- "black"
node.attrs$textCol <- "black"
node.attrs$fontsize <- 14

# Node fill colours by variable group
node.attrs$fill[c(Geography, Topography)] <- "lightgray"    # geography and topography
node.attrs$fill[Climate]                  <- "lightyellow"  # climate
node.attrs$fill[Subsistence]              <- "lightgreen"   # subsistence strategies
node.attrs$fill[SocialOrg]               <- "lightblue"    # social organisation

nodeRenderInfo(gR) <- node.attrs

# ── Arc appearance ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Arcs with direction < 0.60: dashed (weak directional consensus)
# Arcs with direction >= 0.60: solid  (strong directional consensus)


# Optional: line width scaled by arc strength (used only by the commented-out line below)
lwd_range <- c(1, 6)   # min / max line width
strength_range <- range(selected_arcs$strength)

scale_lwd <- function(s) {
  lwd_range[1] + sqrt((s - strength_range[1]) / diff(strength_range)) * diff(lwd_range)
}


all_arc_names <- names(arc.attrs$lty)

for (k in 1:nrow(selected_arcs)) {
  arc_name <- paste0(selected_arcs$from[k], "~", selected_arcs$to[k])

  if (arc_name %in% all_arc_names) {
    arc.attrs$col[arc_name] <- "black"

    #arc.attrs$col[arc_name] <- ifelse(selected_arcs$strength[k] >= 0.2, "black", "steelblue")

    arc.attrs$lwd[arc_name]=2


    #arc.attrs$lwd[arc_name]      <- scale_lwd(selected_arcs$strength[k])

    arc.attrs$lty[arc_name] <- ifelse(selected_arcs$direction[k] < 0.6,
                                      "dashed", "solid")
    arc.attrs$fontsize[arc_name] <- 10

  }
}

edgeRenderInfo(gR) <- arc.attrs
renderGraph(gR)



# ── Save plots (TIFF, PNG, PDF) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# File names encode the scenario and threshold (e.g. threshold = 0.3 -> "BN_none_thr3")

filename <- paste0("output/BN_", direction, "_thr", as.integer(threshold * 10))

tiff(paste0(filename, ".tif"), res = 300, width = 15, height = 10,
     units = "cm", compression = "lzw", bg = "white", type = "cairo")
renderGraph(gR)
dev.off()


filename <- paste0("output/BN_", direction, "_thr", as.integer(threshold * 10))

png(paste0(filename, ".png"), res = 300, width = 15, height = 10,
    units = "cm", bg = "transparent")
renderGraph(gR)
dev.off()

pdf(paste0(filename, ".pdf"))
renderGraph(gR)
dev.off()
```




# 6. Model fitting: local distribution of each node
```{r}

# Mixed-variable BN:
#   continuous nodes : Gaussian linear regression on parents (lm)
#   discrete nodes   : multinomial logistic regression on parents (nnet::multinom)
# fitted_list stores one fitted model per node.

fitted_list <- list()

# Discrete and continuous nodes present in the consensus DAG
discrete_vars   <- intersect(c("SettlementType", "CommOrg", "HouseholdOrg"),
                             nodes(avg_graph))
continuous_nodes <- setdiff(nodes(avg_graph), discrete_vars)

# ── Continuous nodes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
for (node in continuous_nodes) {
  parents <- parents(avg_graph, node)

  if (length(parents) == 0) {
    # Root node: unconditional mean and SD
    fitted_list[[node]] <- list(
      coef = mean(dat[[node]]),
      sd   = sd(dat[[node]])
    )
  } else {
    # Non-root node: linear regression on parents
    formula_str        <- paste(node, "~", paste(parents, collapse = " + "))
    fitted_list[[node]] <- lm(as.formula(formula_str), data = dat)
  }
}

# ── Discrete nodes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# multinom() allows discrete and continuous parents
library(nnet)

for (node in discrete_vars) {
  parents <- parents(avg_graph, node)

  if (length(parents) == 0) {
    # Root node: empirical marginal distribution
    fitted_list[[node]] <- table(dat[[node]]) / nrow(dat)
  } else {
    # Non-root node: multinomial logistic regression on parents
    formula_str        <- paste(node, "~", paste(parents, collapse = " + "))
    fitted_list[[node]] <- multinom(as.formula(formula_str),
                                    data  = dat,
                                    trace = FALSE)   # suppress iteration output
  }
}
```



# 7. Interventional analysis (do-operator via Monte Carlo simulation)
```{r}
# ── Source functions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

source("fn_simulate_all_Y_interventions.R")
# Functions defined in this file:
#   simulate_all_Y_interventions() : simulations for all intervention variables Y at once
#   simulate_doY_region()          : simulate all nodes under one intervention on Y
#   draw_Y_empirical()             : sample Y from the observed data within the intervention region


source("fn_interventional_analysis_ci.R")
# Functions defined in this file:
#   compute_interventional_analysis_ci()                : main wrapper; all (X, Y) pairs
#   compute_interventional_prob_with_ci()               : P(X | do(Y)) and 95% CI, continuous Y
#   compute_interventional_prob_with_ci_categorical_Y() : P(X | do(Y = k)) and 95% CI, categorical Y
#   create_results_table()                              : results as two data frames (continuous / categorical Y)


# plot_ratio(): bar charts of interventional probability ratios
source("fn_plot_ratio.R")

# ── Outcome variables (X) and intervention variables (Y) ─────────────────────

#Subsistence <- c("Hunt_Agri","Animal_Agri", "Fish_Agri"  , "Gather_Agri" )
#SocialOrg   <- c("CommSize", "SettlementType", "CommOrg", "HouseholdOrg")

# X: Subsistence and SocialOrg variables present in the network
X_vars <- intersect(c(Subsistence, SocialOrg), nodes(avg_graph))

# Y: all ancestors of the X variables in the DAG (upstream causes)
all_ancestors <- unique(unlist(lapply(X_vars, function(x) {
  bnlearn::ancestors(avg_graph, x)
})))



Y_vars <- all_ancestors


# ── Simulate the interventional distribution of X under do(Y) ────────────────

# Intervention values for each Y:
#   continuous Y  : median, giving do(Y <= median) vs do(Y > median)
#   categorical Y : each factor level, giving do(Y = k)
ay_list <- setNames(
  lapply(all_ancestors, function(y) {
    if (is.numeric(dat[[y]])) {
      median(dat[[y]], na.rm = TRUE)   # continuous Y: do(Y > median) vs do(Y <= median)
    } else {
      levels(dat[[y]])                 # discrete Y: do(Y = k) for each category k
    }
  }),
  all_ancestors
)

set.seed(0428)

sim_results <- simulate_all_Y_interventions(
  fitted_list = fitted_list,
  avg_graph   = avg_graph,
  dat         = dat,
  Y_vars      = all_ancestors,
  ay_list     = ay_list,
  n           = 1e6                    # number of Monte Carlo samples
)

# Save / reload simulation results (large object)
#saveRDS(sim_results, file = paste0("sim_results_", out_label, ".rds"), compress = TRUE)
# sim_results <- readRDS("sim_results.rds")


# ── Interventional probabilities, ratios and 95% CIs ─────────────────────────

# Event on each X:
#   continuous X  : {X > median}
#   categorical X : {X = k} for each level k
ax_list <- setNames(
  lapply(X_vars, function(x) {
    if (is.numeric(dat[[x]])) {
      median(dat[[x]], na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      levels(dat[[x]])
    }
  }),
  X_vars
)


results <- compute_interventional_analysis_ci(
  sim_results = sim_results,
  avg_graph   = avg_graph,
  dat         = dat,
  X_vars      = X_vars,
  ax_list     = ax_list     # if NULL, the median of each continuous X is used
)

results_tables <- create_results_table(results, digits = 3)

# ── Save interventional results ──────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!is.null(results_tables$continuous_Y)) {
  fname=paste0("output/intervention_conti_Y_thr", as.integer(threshold*10),
               "_", out_label, ".csv"  )
  write.csv(results_tables$continuous_Y,
            fname, row.names = FALSE)
}
if (!is.null(results_tables$categorical_Y)) {
  fname=paste0("output/intervention_cat_Y_thr", as.integer(threshold*10),
               "_", out_label, ".csv")
  write.csv(results_tables$categorical_Y,
            fname, row.names = FALSE)
}

# ── Plot interventional probability ratios ───────────────────────────────────

# Label each (X, Y) result as an increase (ratio > 1) or decrease
results_tables$continuous_Y$ratio_ind <- ifelse(
  results_tables$continuous_Y$ratio > 1, "Increase", "Decrease"
)

# Subsistence and SocialOrg outcomes present in the results,
# with Subsistence in a fixed display order
desired_order          <- c("Hunt_Agri", "Animal_Agri","Fish_Agri",  "Gather_Agri")
Subsistence_in_network <- desired_order[desired_order %in%
                                          intersect(results_tables$continuous_Y$X, Subsistence)]
SocialOrg_in_network   <- intersect(results_tables$continuous_Y$X, SocialOrg)

# Fixed level order for categorical variables in the plots
dat$HouseholdOrg <- factor(  dat$HouseholdOrg,
  levels = c("Large extended", "Small extended", "Nuclear")
)

dat$SettlementType <- factor(  dat$SettlementType,
  levels = c("Village", "Homesteads", "Hamlet")
)

plot_ratio(results_tables, Subsistence_in_network, SocialOrg_in_network, out_label)
#plot_ratio_strength(results_tables, strength_df= selected_arcs, Subsistence_in_network, SocialOrg_in_network)

```

# Custom BIC for mixed data (fn_comp_BIC.R); lower is better
source("fn_comp_BIC.R")

BIC <- compute_custom_bic(avg_graph, dat, verbose = FALSE)

filename <- paste0("output/BIC_", out_label, "_thr", as.integer(threshold * 10), ".csv")

write.csv(BIC, filename)
